lesson.title: Guitar Conversations
lesson.complete_text:
You can make clean notes and move between them.

Both hands working together - right hand creating sound, left hand changing pitch.

FOUNDATION COMPLETE

Seven layers. Each one builds on the last.
How to Learn -> Language -> Music -> Guitar -> The Instrument -> Speaking -> Conversations

Next: Doing - alternate picking, chromatic exercises, hammer-ons, your first scales.

steps.text:
You can make a clean note. Good. But music isn't one note - it's notes moving.

This is the last block of Foundation. After this, you're ready for everything that comes next.

The moment you play one note, then another, you've created an interval - the distance between two sounds.

This is the DNA of melody. Every song ever written is just intervals - sequences of distances between notes.

The real skill isn't playing one note. It's moving from one note to the next cleanly.

response.text: Yes. Every riff, every solo, every melody is just a sequence of intervals. You're about to play your first ones.

reexplain.text: Chords come later. Right now we're talking about melody - notes played one after another.
Melody is built from intervals - the distance from one note to the next. Chords are notes played simultaneously. Intervals are the DNA of melody. Chords are the harmony.
So what is the DNA of melody?

steps.text:
Here's your first real exercise. Put both hands together:

1. Pick the 3rd string (G) - play it open
2. Press fret 2 with your index finger (behind the fret wire)
3. Pick it again
4. Lift your finger. Play open again.

Open -> Fret 2 -> Open. That's a whole step up, then back down. Your first two-note sequence.

Do it 10 times. Listen: does each note ring clean? Is the transition smooth?
What interval did you just play (open to fret 2)?

choices.label: A whole step - two frets up

response.text: Yes! Fret 0 to fret 2 = two frets = whole step. You just played a real interval with your own hands. Theory you can feel.

choices.label: A half step - one fret up

reexplain.text: Open is fret 0. You pressed fret 2. That's two frets = two half steps = one whole step. A half step would be fret 0 to fret 1.
So what interval is open to fret 2?

steps.text:
Now let's walk. Same string, one fret at a time:

Open -> Fret 1 -> Fret 2 -> Fret 3 -> Fret 4

Right hand picks. Left hand frets. One at a time. Slow and clean.

Now walk back: Fret 4 -> Fret 3 -> Fret 2 -> Fret 1 -> Open

This is the fundamental movement of guitar - fingers walking along a string. Every scale, every riff, every melody is built from this.

Try it on a different string tomorrow. Then another. One string per day. Within a week, your hands will start to know the fretboard.

You're not just learning exercises. You're building the foundation of every technique you'll ever use.

You now have the seven layers of Foundation. But Foundation is not the end - it's the launchpad.

What comes next is Doing. That's where your hands start training for real. You'll meet:

Alternate picking - down-up-down-up, the picking foundation. Clean, even, rhythmic.

Chromatic exercises - fingers 1-2-3-4 across all strings. Building independence and strength.

Hammer-ons and pull-offs - legato technique. Smooth, connected notes without picking every one.

Your first scales - pentatonic shapes. The vocabulary of rock, blues, and pop.

Everything you learned in Foundation - the body scan, the two strokes, the fretting position, the intervals - feeds directly into these techniques. Nothing was wasted.
You just played open -> fret 2 -> open. What technique will you learn first in Doing?

choices.label: Alternate picking - down-up-down-up on a single string

response.text: Yes! Alternate picking is the foundation of all picking technique. You already know how to pluck a string. Now you'll learn to do it in a steady, even rhythm - down, up, down, up. Ready for the next level.

reexplain.text: Barre chords come later - they require finger strength you're still building.
The first technique in Doing is alternate picking - the down-up motion on a single string. It's the foundation of all picking technique. Barre chords come after you've built finger independence.
So what technique will you learn first?
Sweep picking is advanced - it comes much later.
Alternate picking is first. Down-up-down-up on a single string. Clean, even, rhythmic. This is the technique that every other picking style builds on.

steps.text:
You can make clean notes and move between them.

Both hands working together - right hand creating sound, left hand changing pitch.

You can walk up and down a string. You've played your first intervals.

FOUNDATION COMPLETE

Seven layers. Each one builds on the last.
How to Learn -> Language -> Music -> Guitar -> The Instrument -> Speaking -> Conversations

You now have the foundation for everything that comes next.
